assumptions.ruleset: Gathering Storm with every expansion and the Leader Pass
assumptions.map: Continents or Pangaea, standard size, 8 civilizations
assumptions.notes: Turn numbers are Standard-speed scaffolding; the site rescales them for other speeds and difficulties. Lady Six Sky's single persona is planned here. The shape is Front-Load because the whole empire is measured from the capital tile, the capital cannot be moved, and the number of city sites inside six tiles of it is fixed the turn the Settler plants.

verdict.one_line: Plant the capital where eight cities fit inside six tiles, settle all of them by turn 70 on Farms and Plantations rather than rivers, put an Observatory beside the Plantations in every one, and let a compact empire at +10% to everything out-research rivals twice its size.
verdict.why: Ix Mutal Ajaw gives every other city within six tiles of the capital a tenth more of every yield and takes 15% away from anything farther, so the empire is a circle drawn on turn one and the only question is how many cities the circle holds. Mayab removes the need for rivers and coasts: Farms give Housing and Gold, so cities sit wherever the circle needs them, three tiles apart on dry land, and the Farms they grow on are Observatory adjacency. The Observatory takes major adjacency from Plantations and minor from Farms and districts, which a packed circle supplies without a mountain in sight. Science is the victory because the kit's yield is Science and the circle's weakness is scale, which Science punishes least. Culture is the fallback because the same compact Theater Squares get the same +10%. Domination fights the kit: a captured city outside the circle is a liability at -15%.

must_have: Flat or hill land, not ocean, mountain or marsh, for at least six city centers at three-tile spacing inside six tiles of the start, counted on the visible map before the Settler moves.
Two or more Plantation resources (Bananas, Sugar, Spices, Cotton, Silk, Dyes, Citrus, Cocoa, Coffee, Tea, Tobacco, Olives) inside the circle for the Observatories.
prefer: Grassland and plains rather than hills under the circle: Farms are the Housing, the Gold and the adjacency, and they need flat land.
Luxury resources adjacent to the planned city centers; Mayab gives an Amenity for each one touching the center.
Rainforest at the edge of the circle for a Holy Site and late appeal; it is cleared for Farms inside.
Ik Kil, Roraima or the Fountain of Youth inside the circle; each is a Science or district bonus the capital can own.
map_check.no_go: A start on a peninsula, an island or a coast-and-mountain pocket where fewer than five city centers fit inside six tiles of any reachable tile. The circle then holds a capital and three satellites, the +10% multiplies almost nothing, and Maya is a civ with a good Archer.
map_check.fallback: If the visible land is cramped but open country is within three tiles, walk the Settler up to three turns to center the circle on it; a turn-4 capital with eight sites beats a turn-1 capital with four. If nothing within three turns holds six sites, settle, draw the circle anyway, fill every site it has, and plan a Culture game from wonders in a tall capital rather than a Science game from city count; say plainly that the ceiling is five cities and that the game is won by turn 250 or not at all.

kit_levers.name: Ix Mutal Ajaw
kit_levers.buys: Every yield in non-capital cities within six tiles of the Capital is raised by a tenth and every yield in cities farther away is cut by more; units within six tiles of the Capital fight at +5 Combat Strength.
kit_levers.exploit: The capital tile is chosen for the circle it draws, not for the tile itself. Every city is founded inside the circle, at three-tile spacing so that eight to ten fit; none is founded outside it for any resource, wonder or coast. The defence is a ring of Hul'che inside the circle where they already have +5; nothing is built to fight beyond it.

kit_levers.name: Mayab
kit_levers.buys: Cities get no Housing from fresh water or coast, but every Farm gives Housing and Gold, and each Luxury resource adjacent to a City Center gives an Amenity.
kit_levers.exploit: Rivers and lakes are ignored when drawing the circle; Farms are placed in triangles around each center so that every city has six or more by turn 80, which is Housing for twelve, Gold for Builders, and the Feudalism Inspiration. City centers are placed touching a Luxury where one exists, because the Amenity is free and the compact empire runs short of them.

kit_levers.name: Hul'che
kit_levers.buys: An Archer replacement with higher Ranged Strength and a bonus against units that are already wounded.
kit_levers.exploit: Three of them, built at Archery and kept inside the circle, are the whole Ancient and Classical army: with +5 from the capital and the wounded bonus they finish anything a Warrior has touched. They also give the Machinery Eureka as Archers. The plan builds three and upgrades them, nothing more.

kit_levers.name: Observatory
kit_levers.buys: A Campus replacement whose adjacency comes from Plantations and from Farms and districts rather than from mountains, reefs and rainforest.
kit_levers.exploit: Placed in every city on the tile touching the most Plantations, and otherwise between the Farm triangles so that four Farms, the City Center and one more district give it +3. Its tile is pinned at settle time, because the Farms around it are placed to feed it. Natural Philosophy doubles whatever it has, and every city has one by turn 100.

kit_levers.name: Solitary
kit_levers.buys: Lady Six Sky likes leaders who settle far from her and dislikes those who settle near her borders.
kit_levers.exploit: Irrelevant to your own play except as a warning: an AI Lady Six Sky on the map will forward-settle nobody and will hate anyone who crowds her circle, so leave her the land she wants and she is the safest neighbour on the roster.

turn_zero: Before the Settler moves: count the city centers that fit at three-tile spacing inside six tiles of the start on land you can see or reasonably infer. Six or more is a go. Four or five: move up to three turns toward open land and count again. Fewer: run the fallback.

Before the Settler moves: ignore the river. Mayab gives no Housing from it; the capital goes where the circle is largest, which is usually one or two tiles inland from where the game placed the Settler.

Before the Settler moves: find the Plantations. Each is an Observatory anchor; a capital with two Plantation resources within its first two rings has a +4 Observatory before any Farm. Pin the capital's Observatory on the tile that touches them, and the Farm triangles around it.

By turn 10: draw the circle. Every city site at three-tile spacing inside six tiles of the capital, numbered in the order they will be settled, each with its Observatory tile pinned. The count is the empire; write it down.
front_load.ceiling: Eight to ten cities inside the circle, each reaching 12 to 15 population on Farm Housing, each with an Observatory at +3 to +5 and a Commercial Hub, at +10% to everything. That is a Science victory around turn 260 on Emperor from Universities and Research Labs in every city and Spaceport projects in the two biggest, with Culture close behind from the same +10% on Theater Squares. The cap is land: the circle holds what it holds, no conquest adds to it, and the Mars projects run on nine cities' Production and Gold, not on twenty. The plan accepts the cap and buys what it cannot build.

irreversibles.decision: Capital tile: the circle is drawn from it and nothing founded outside the circle will ever be at full yield.
Capital Observatory tile pinned beside the Plantations, with the Farm triangles drawn around it; a Farm or district on the wrong tile costs adjacency for the game.
The circle map: every site numbered, every Observatory tile named, before the second Settler is produced. A site skipped for a better one outside the circle is a city lost.
The rule for cities that are not yours: anything captured or flipped outside the circle is razed or liberated, never kept; written down before the first war is declared on you.

front_load.settle_map_rule: Draw every city before the second Settler is produced: a grid of centers exactly three tiles apart filling the circle of radius six around the capital, on flat or hill land, with no regard to rivers, lakes or coast. Number the sites by distance from the capital and settle them in that order so that the inner ring exists before a rival can reach it. Pin each site's Observatory on the tile touching the most Plantations, or failing that the tile where four Farms and the center can surround it. Mark the Farm triangles so no Builder mines a tile that was a Farm. A site at distance seven is not a site, however rich; a site at distance six on plain grassland is settled over it every time. Luxuries adjacent to a center are preferred for the Amenity, and the center is shifted one tile to touch one only if the shift keeps it inside the circle and keeps the three-tile spacing.

phases.name: Assess and commit
phases.objective: Plant the capital where the circle is largest, pin its Observatory and Farm triangles, draw and number every site in the circle, found the pantheon, and have two Settlers out and the first Hul'che standing by turn 20. The twenty turns that fix the size of the empire.

Site two, on the far side of the capital; Religious Settlements has given a third by now.
Culture for Early Empire and Political Philosophy; a Farm capital grows faster than its civics.
Two more at Archery; with +5 inside the circle they hold the rim against anything Ancient.
The capital's, on the pinned tile the turn Writing lands; +4 from two Plantations before any Farm.

checkpoints.pass: Continue; number the sites before the Settler finishes.
checkpoints.fail: Fewer than five sites: the fallback applies and the plan is a five-city Culture game from here. Observatory unpinned: pin it this turn, before the Builder farms the tile it should sit on.

checkpoints.pass: Enter the circle phase and settle in number order.
checkpoints.fail: No numbered map: draw it this turn. A Settler walking to a site outside the circle: turn it round; the -15% is permanent and a worse site inside is better than a better site outside.

tasks.text: Count the three-tile sites inside six tiles; plant where the count is highest, up to three turns' walk, ignoring the river.
Pin the capital Observatory on the tile touching the most Plantations and draw the two Farm triangles around the center.
Scout the rim of the circle; mark Plantations, Luxuries beside planned centers, and the one camp inside the circle.
Number every site in the circle by distance from the capital, with its Observatory tile; write the total. That number is the empire.
Found Religious Settlements; send the free Settler to site three.
Archery in: upgrade the Slinger and build two more Hul'che; station them at the rim between the capital and the nearest rival.

city_states.why: Growth 15% faster in cities with a Campus, and the Observatory counts; nine cities grow on Farms 15% faster.

checkpoints.fail: Sites unsettled because a rival took them: the circle is smaller than drawn; write the new count and raise the Culture fallback's weight. Observatories unbuilt: they are the first district everywhere and nothing is queued ahead of them.

phases.name: The compact core
phases.objective: Nine cities out-yield fifteen: Universities on every Observatory, Commercial Hubs and Markets everywhere for the Gold that buys what the land cannot build, Theater Squares in the inner ring for the Culture fallback, Industrial Zones in the two biggest, and an Entertainment Complex or the Colosseum for the Amenities a dense empire runs short of. The Hul'che become Crossbowmen and stay home.

Seven district types; the Entertainment Complex and a rim Holy Site make it; an Aqueduct does not count.
The capital at fifteen population.
Astronomy is taken late; usually unboosted.
A Neighborhood on a Breathtaking rim tile.
An Archaeological Museum if the capital Theater Square has the Production spare.
Research Radio first; the Inspiration follows at no extra cost.

decision_triggers.name: A rival Settler heads for the circle
decision_triggers.if: A foreign Settler is seen walking toward a numbered site that is not yet settled.
decision_triggers.then: The next Settler goes to that site out of number order, escorted by a Hul'che; a Warrior stands on the site tile until it arrives. A rival city inside the circle is a permanent hole in the empire and a loyalty war you cannot afford.

decision_triggers.name: A city flips to you
decision_triggers.if: A rival city outside six tiles joins you through Loyalty or is offered in a peace deal.
decision_triggers.then: Apply the written rule: raze it if it is small, liberate it if it was ever someone else's, keep it only if it holds a wonder or a strategic resource the circle lacks, as a no-district Production city. The -15% is forever and so is the war it attracts.

decision_triggers.name: Amenities turn negative
decision_triggers.if: Three or more cities show negative Amenities at any point after turn 90.
decision_triggers.then: Stop district construction in those cities and build the Entertainment Complex or buy the Arena; a compact empire shares Luxuries badly and the +10% is lost to unrest faster than it is gained. Shift a center onto a Luxury only when founding, never after.

decision_triggers.name: An army arrives at the rim
decision_triggers.if: A rival force crosses into the circle before turn 150.
decision_triggers.then: Do not build Walls everywhere. The Hul'che and later the Crossbowmen fight at +5 inside the circle; pull them back two tiles so the enemy is wounded by the city and finished by the wounded bonus. Nothing pursues past the rim.

abort.trigger: Turn 20 with a capital whose circle holds fewer than five sites and no better capital within reach, or turn 80 with three or more cities founded outside six tiles.
actions: Say plainly that the circle is small and that the empire is the cities inside it; stop founding cities for land the ability punishes.

Switch the weight to Culture: a tall capital with the Pyramids, the Colosseum, Kilwa and the Hermitage, Theater Squares in every inner city, and Faith-bought Great Artists, aiming to finish before the capped Science would.
Raze or liberate the outside cities before they become the war; keep the Hul'che line and the +5 inside the circle as the whole defence.

fail_state: Turn 150 with five cities inside the circle and three outside it at -15%, Observatories placed beside rivers for Housing that Mayab never gives, Farms mined for Production, and Science in the middle of the table. The capital tile that drew the circle and the Settlers that left it were decided before turn 40 and no city can be moved.
common_mistakes: Settling the capital on the river. Mayab gives no Housing from water; the Farms give it, and the capital belongs wherever the six-tile circle holds the most cities.
Founding a seventh city two tiles outside the circle because the land is better. It yields 15% less of everything for the game and the city inside on worse land yields a tenth more.
Keeping a captured or flipped city outside the radius because it is free. It is a -15% city that invites a war the Hul'che cannot fight at full strength.
Mining the hills before farming the flats. Farms are the Housing, the Gold and the Observatory adjacency; Mines are a few Production in an empire that buys with Gold.
Placing the Observatory beside the mountain or the reef. It gets nothing from either; it gets Science from Plantations, Farms and districts, and its tile is chosen for those.
sources: Civilization VI Civilopedia, Gathering Storm ruleset with the New Frontier Pass (Maya, Lady Six Sky, Observatory, Hul'che, Mayab, Ix Mutal Ajaw).

Where the civ-info text is thin, the game is followed: Ix Mutal Ajaw is +10% to all yields in non-capital cities within six tiles of the Capital and -15% beyond, with +5 Combat Strength for units within six tiles; Mayab also grants +1 Amenity per Luxury resource adjacent to a City Center; the Observatory's major adjacency is from Plantations and its minor adjacency from Farms and districts, with none from Mountains, Reefs or Rainforest.
